transport.framing: Existing GATT acknowledged stream and uint32-big-endian application length, unchanged
transport.integers: JSON integer lexemes only: no boolean, float, exponent, coercion, duplicate names, NaN or Infinity
transport.rpc_v1: bootstrap.claim and bootstrap.status exact existing v1 shapes/responses remain unchanged on bootstrap profile
transport.rpc_v2: No v2 setup request except negotiate before this exact TLS peer negotiated v2; next_step never triggers a mutation

utc_seconds.narrower_policy: ipc-contract.json exact accepted clock policy applies; representation bound is not UTC authority

country.semantic: Explicit phone choice; exact OS policy and observed firmware/kernel/channel agreement required; no default

authorization.before_each_request: Fresh main writer/admission guard and credential epoch; reopen prepared binding; factory ledger v2 ADOPTED and same first_owner_id; owners.status(owner_id, owner_token, request_id=claim_request_id)
authorization.before_each_new_effect: Same live local peer generation and current OS session, admission and epoch; failure closes admission
authorization.before_delivery: Same peer/lock/workflow generation; stale completion is retained durably but not delivered to a different session
authorization.local_context: Server-generated session_id UUID and monotone generation in a handler closure per actual TLS peer; never supplied/authorized by RESET nonce or JSON
authorization.draining: Never cancel/abandon an admitted syscall/subprocess/thread. After invalidation, no later sub-effect is admitted; partial operation becomes uncertain as specified by OS.
authorization.setup_socket: One persistent OS IPC connection per authorized local peer context; close it on every invalidation

clock_and_retry.apply_ack: Register the immutable apply task in OperationRegistry without awaiting the up-to-45-second OS apply. Return apply_ack_result promptly within the existing 20-second client RPC budget. registered means owned in memory, not OS durability. Worker checkpoints the exact original intent/UTC before IPC submission; status readonly observes progress. Disconnect never abandons the owned worker.
clock_and_retry.client_checkpoint: Client durably saves operation/challenge identifiers before challenge and exact apply UTC/country intent before apply. Retry preserves the identical UTC and intent; never silently resample UTC. Missing checkpoint recovers latest_operation_id via owner/init-scoped OS inspect during negotiate, then polls readonly status; a new real attempt requires explicit fresh operation/challenge.
clock_and_retry.negotiate_discovery: latest_operation_id is obtained from successful readonly setup.inspect scoped to this verified initialization/owner/claim. null means proven not_started, not an inspect failure. unavailable/contradictory inspection refuses rather than inventing an operation or authority.
clock_and_retry.nonce: OS CSPRNG 32 bytes; boot-bound CLOCK_BOOTTIME challenge, not client RESET nonce
clock_and_retry.utc_semantics: Phone samples UTC seconds immediately before constructing apply after receiving the challenge. It is authorized claimed UTC, not independent time-source verification.
clock_and_retry.same_op_same_intent: Return same durable result; never extend challenge expiry or replay an uncertain effect
clock_and_retry.supersede: New explicit op_id with supersedes_op_id; only after old operation is drained and OS has observed prior effects and closed radio; new live owner/claim/session/current-boot challenge required
clock_and_retry.status: Read-only history, never a grant to set time/publish a new certificate or reuse old BOOTTIME

transition.initial_publication: Only PreparedFactoryIdentity.publish_initial, using validated real current-boot OS clock result; no ClockResult from network JSON or historical status alone
transition.same_identity: Keep frame UUID, P256 key and SPKI; completion binds initial publication identity/op, not an immutable current DER
transition.handoff: Close bootstrap admission, complete registered work, then stop old transport before normal TLS. Reuse one display, ownership store v2 and current writer lease; do not close store/display during transfer or call legacy selection.
transition.normal_status: The v2 negotiation/challenge/apply/status/continue service is also available to the admitted owner on normal profile for interrupted continuation, without rescanning QR
transition.normal_wifi: Reuse existing normal Wi-Fi operations through injected NetworkClient(peer_guard=proof.network_guard), then HTTPS /api/provisioning/wifi/confirm with owner headers
transition.completion: Backend requests OS setup.complete only after real network committed inspection and current normal identity binding. Initial publication_op_id is historical and may DIFFER from the current recovery setup op_id; require same initialization lineage/frame UUID/SPKI and real completed explicitly admitted setup effects, without recertification. See IPC contract.
transition.continue: Explicit DATA-ONLY mutation after fresh owner/claim/epoch/session/admission checks. Finalize only an existing durable certificate candidate at identical bytes/intent, or an idempotent root completion backed by real committed network facts. Never clock/country/radio replay, never generate a new candidate from historical status, never restore an old leaf over a renewed current leaf. No candidate plus lost clock context/boot returns recovery_required and requires a new explicit setup operation.
transition.network_changes: NORMAL completion does not pin the original transaction/profile forever. Follow inspect_latest_committed from the actually attested helper process, parse strictly, independently check persisted NM profile/interface/country and atomically update the root-owned network-head. This is not a cryptographic signature claim about helper journal bytes. At gated reboot ipv4=[] is allowed before activation; network_ready requires actual activation/IP. An absent/pending/uncertain helper journal never selects an arbitrary profile or falls back to the old initial profile; keep NORMAL_RECOVERY with WLAN closed, photo/identity/owners preserved.

factory_photo_enrollment.transport: Actual HTTPS only; no forwarded-scheme trust
checks: Current owner/claim/epoch via owners.status; first_owner_id same
OS completion + current normal branch and frame/SPKI bound
device_id differs from BLE owner_id; device_token differs from owner_token
No cookie authorizes enrollment; no password login
factory_photo_enrollment.persistence: Existing PhotoAccessStore.enroll(device_id,device_token,request_id=claim_request_id) under authorization gate; one idempotent credential per factory claim without a new PHOTO schema
factory_photo_enrollment.next: Client already persisted a NEW PHOTO secret before request, then calls existing HTTPS device-session; no cookie issued by factory enroll
factory_photo_enrollment.media: Existing media/invitation route scope unchanged; never promote a media/device cookie or reuse BLE secret

origin.lan_gate: For status/continue results that require a LAN transition, https_origin=null forces next_step=wait_origin and readonly polling. Never confirm Wi-Fi or enroll PHOTO over LAN until the explicit origin is verified. While waiting, current-owner BLE Wi-Fi scan/begin/status remain available on normal profile; wait_origin is not a ban on configuring Wi-Fi and cannot create a pre-IP deadlock.
origin.factory: OS observes existing persisted inky-<32hex>.local hostname using rootstate/etc hostname + Avahi GetHostNameFqdn/GetState + current interfaces/NM; returns explicit https_origin or null
origin.backend: Inject a factory origin provider bound to current attestation/boot and identity. Never synthesize from Host, SAN, socket.gethostname or unauthenticated IP; do not mutate process environment.
origin.invitation: public_identity(with_url=True) uses the explicit verified factory origin in factory mode; absent/unverified origin refuses invitation creation
